title: Paths in Matrix Whose Sum Is Divisible by K
summary: Given a matrix grid and an integer k, count the number of paths from (0,0) to (m-1,n-1) where the sum of elements on the path is divisible by k, modulo 10^9 + 7.
statement: Given a matrix grid and an integer k, count the number of paths from (0,0) to (m-1,n-1) where the sum of elements on the path is divisible by k, modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: grid is a nonempty rectangular matrix and rows*columns is at most 50000.
Move only right or down from the top-left to the bottom-right cell.
Return modulo 1,000,000,007 the number of paths whose inclusive cell sum is divisible by k.
hints: Path counts need the sum remainder, not the potentially enormous full sum.
For every cell, store one count per remainder and extend states from its top and left neighbors.
For desired remainder r, add predecessor remainder (r-cell_value) mod k from both directions.
Every right/down path reaches a cell from exactly one of those two predecessors; the remainder transition preserves its sum, so the destination remainder-zero count is exact.
editorial: Every right/down path reaches a cell from exactly one of those two predecessors; the remainder transition preserves its sum, so the destination remainder-zero count is exact.

tests.explanation: Exactly two right/down paths have sums divisible by three.
The only path sums to zero, which is divisible by five.
